newsitem.title: CHILE: Minority of Escondida miners confirm Friday strike.
newsitem.headline: Minority of Escondida miners confirm Friday strike.

text.p: A group of about 300 unionized workers at the Escondida copper mine in northern Chile have voted to strike as of 8 a.m. (1300 GMT) on Friday, a union leader said.
Union leaders earlier said they were certain that the strike had been approved by the workers -- who make up only about 15 percent of Escondida's total work force of nearly 2,000 people.

"The vote was 93 votes in favour of accepting the company's latest offer and 206 in favour of the strike," said union leader Hugo Fernandez. "Tomorrow (on Wednesday) we will begin the task of making management more sensitive to our requests."
Escondida officials were not available for comment on the strike's potential effects on production.
But leaders of the mine's small union admitted there was no sign of other workers joining the walkout for wage increases.

"Will they support or participate in the strike? No. But there may be ways for them to cooperate," said Fernandez, speaking to Reuters by telephone from the city of Antofagasta. He declined to elaborate.
The workers who voted to strike were in various parts of the vast Escondida mining complex, said Fernandez.
"We're in the mine, in the plant and at Puerto Coloso," he said.

Puerto Coloso is where Escondida, owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ Corp plc, ships out its cathodes and concentrates. The copper mine, the world's largest, produced over 800,000 tonnes of the red metal last year.
